title: Gonna discect all the symbolism from the Bad Bunny halftime show like...
transcript: Good storytelling transcends language. I don't understand Spanish. I still got the gist of what Bad Bunny was trying to say with that halftime show. And before I watched the halftime show, I saw the matinee of godspeed at the Denver Center. And one of the characters in this, like, really fun western revenge story spoke entirely in Spanish for the most part. And all of the conversations that she had with another character, she would speak in Spanish and the other character would speak in English. So I only understood about half the conversation, and yet I still understood what was going on because the storytelling was that strong. Even children's media is often silent. It's all silent storytelling, and yet you're still able to understand the story that is happening. I think that we as English speakers often take for granted that, you know, we. We are spoon fed through language what stories are trying to say. And maybe that's why media literacy is at an all time low, is because we haven't had to work for finding the symbolism and finding the nuances and. And parsing together what a story is about, because we constantly are seeing media in our own language, and so people are just directly telling us what their story is about. And so maybe, maybe for the sake of media literacy, we need more Spanish storytelling. And also, so many people in the United States speak Spanish anyway, so, you know, may Maybe it could be beneficial for everyone. Anyway, loved the half time show. And godspeed at the Denver Center. Also really good.
classificationReason: Primarily a meditation on storytelling and media literacy prompted by the Bad Bunny Super Bowl halftime show. Briefly mentions seeing 'Godspeed at the Denver Center,' which is not on the list. No review of any listed stage production.
